description: Closed-hem flat-pattern golden for an AUTHORED plate + one CLOSED HEM (docs/design/sheet-metal-parity.md §2 Hem row / Parity roadmap #3; docs/design/sheet-metal.md §1/§4.2/§9). A closed hem folds the picked edge ~180 deg back FLAT onto the parent face, so its two layers very nearly touch. Rebuilt from a real feature tree (sketch -> sheet_metal_base_flange -> sheet_metal_hem), tagged with a CylindricalFaceSignature at construction, and found back by that signature (never blind detection). Proves the near-flat 180-deg fold produces ONE clean valid solid and develops correctly (BA = pi*(r + K*t)), i.e. the closed hem reuses the edge-flange bend + unfold machinery verbatim. HEM-1 (2026-08-28): this model takes the DEFAULT radius — it carries no `bend_radius_mm` at all — because the defect it now guards was a DEFAULT-behaviour defect. The previous revision overrode the radius to 1.0 mm, i.e. it could not have failed for the reason this golden exists.
tangent_line_convention: Flat length is measured to the bend TANGENT LINES (§9 #1). The base flange's developed leg is the full length of its flat top face (50 mm, from the far edge to the bend tangent line at the hemmed edge); the hem return's developed leg is its own flat face length (15 mm). The bend allowance BA REPLACES the two setback segments a sharp-corner unfold would use. A closed hem is a 180-deg fold, so the developed strip is the SAME kind of BA strip any bend produces; its bend-table row reads angle 180 deg.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill). Dims: base flange 50 x 20 mm (developed leg 50, width 20), hem return developed leg 15 mm, gauge t = 2 mm, fold angle 180 deg = pi, K = 0.44 (v1 default).

HEM RADIUS (HEM-1): the model sets NO bend_radius_mm, so the radius comes from the hem TYPE and the GAUGE — r = HEM_CLOSED_RADIUS_RATIO * t = 0.05 * 2 = 0.1 mm — and NOT from the part's general base-flange radius (3.0 mm, still set on the base flange in model.json precisely so this golden proves the hem does not reach for it). The fold's cross-section makes the layers' air gap exactly 2*r, so the old inheritance produced a 6.00 mm gap — three gauges of air — inside a hem labelled 'closed'.

AIR GAP (the property the hem's NAME asserts): gap = 2*r = 0.2 mm = 0.1 x gauge. Measured on the built solid as the distance from the hem's parent flat (its recorded base_face_signature plane) to the nearest face that faces back at it: 0.20000000000000107 mm, residual 1.05e-15 vs analytic.
Flat length (§9 #1): flat_length = base_leg + BA + hem_leg = 50 + 3.0787608005179972 + 15 = 68.078760800518 mm. Measured == analytic (residual 0.0).

Developed area (§9 #2, neutral-surface conservation): flat_area = base_area + hem_area + BA*width = (50*20) + (15*20) + (3.0787608005179972*20) = 1000 + 300 + 61.575216... = 1361.57521601036 mm^2. Equivalently flat_length * width (the blank is a rectangle).

Fold direction is inferred from the geometry (§5): the hem return folds to the +normal side of the base flange, so direction = 'up'. Fold angle = 180 deg exactly (the return's flat face normal is anti-parallel to the base's -> dot -1.0 -> acos = pi to full precision).

Fused body volume = base plate (50*20*2 = 2000) + hem return (cross-section 15*2 + half-annulus (pi/2)((r+t)^2 - r^2) = (pi/2)((2.1)^2 - (0.1)^2) = (pi/2)*4.4; cross-section = 30 + 6.9115038378975445 = 36.911503837897545, * 20 width = 738.23007675795089) = 2738.2300767579509 mm^3 (analytic). The return sits 2*r = 0.2 mm above the base, so the fold-back does NOT self-intersect and the two layers are NOT coincident: 0.2 mm is 2000x the kernel's 1e-4 mm linear tolerance, so find_zero_width_slits reports nothing.

content_hash is the sha256 of the provenance-driven FlatPattern.to_json_bytes(). It is a DETERMINISM PIN (byte-identity), not analytic -- reproducible in-process AND across a fresh interpreter restart (§9 #4). Version-pinned like the STEP/PDF export goldens: a change WITHOUT a kernel-version bump is a determinism regression (P0), never a retry.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill). Measured deviations vs the hand-derived values (2026-08-28, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9): flat_length residual 0.0, flat_area residual 0.0, BA residual 1.78e-15, resolved inner radius residual 5.27e-16. Documented ceiling 1e-9 gives ample headroom for platform FP variation while staying tighter than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m). The volume tolerance (1e-6) absorbs arc-fit noise scaled by the 20 mm width (measured residual 9.09e-13).
air_gap_rationale: Measured first, then set. The gap is a difference of two parallel plane offsets on axis-aligned geometry; the measured residual vs the analytic 2*r is 1.05e-15 mm. The 1e-12 ceiling is ~3 orders above that worst observed residual and 8 orders BELOW the kernel's 1e-4 mm linear tolerance, so it can neither drift into a false failure nor admit a gap the kernel would consider a different place. NOT an ad-hoc epsilon: it is derived from a measurement of this model, and it is the tolerance on the one property the hem's name asserts.
